I used the fetch from decision D-17, not the analyst's local-refs-only proposal.

push_bookkeeping returns a PushResult (a str with .status pushed|side|local|failed and .branch). When the release branch may not take the push, the same commit goes to origin/brain/wip by plain push (brain/wip-<session> if that cannot fast-forward), the release branch is untouched, and newer_checkpoints finds it. `checkpoint --push` exits 0 only when the state is on the remote. Not in my files: init still leaves its own files uncommitted (contract.py, package B); the first checkpoint now says so and gives the commit to make.

In bootstrap or adopt mode boot replaces the init hint when a remote branch holds a state, and names the branch and item; `brain resume --adopt` works without --project in a checkout that is not managed yet. Handover's line to paste is now `Continue (branch <name>)` (it routes as resume).

Same defect as core-01, fixed once. Also: `brain status` ends with the GitHub address of STATUS.md on the branch that holds the state (credentials in the remote address are never printed). The skill and guide sentences are listed under instruction_notes.

Bookkeeping is an allow-list (state.BOOK_FILES, BOOK_DIRS with record file types only) passed to git add and git commit as explicit paths. The manifest, .brain/ext and anything else under .brain/ are left for their author; the count is true and up to three files are named. release_branch_block covers rule pr as well as main-on-green. Handover names the uncommitted files.

state.state_problem reports a missing file, a damaged byte, conflict markers and an empty or cut file. Boot and resume print it as a PROBLEM line; checkpoint raises StateError and writes nothing (exit 1, one line with the git command). read_state decodes with errors=replace. A missing file may be created again. No --force flag: deleting the file is the way to start over. contract.validate does not call it yet (package B).

Boot builds (priority, line) pairs, clips every line by bytes, fills by priority within 1,500 bytes and 15 lines, skips a line that does not fit instead of stopping, and ends with `… N more line(s) left out: brain resume` when anything was dropped. Title, folder name and the attached list are clipped.

Every not-pushed outcome is one line with the next step and a non-zero exit: no repository, no remote, detached HEAD, no author identity, rejected push (git pull --rebase), timeout (no traceback; both pushes guarded). Only existing paths are staged, so a missing NEEDS_YOU.md no longer blocks the commit. Handover is not ready for a project that is not a git repository. A brain commit left unpushed by a failed push is pushed by the next call.

state.notes_tail shows the newest notes first with a count of older ones; boot and resume use it. Notes are capped at 8 and the same note twice in a row is stored once. Resume's first line names the project, the branch and the commits not pushed; file names are shown unquoted; resume stays within 12 lines of 240 characters.

Boot sizes the request with the checkpointed tier, not the manifest's first one. Handover releases the lease (session: none) before the push, so the next boot has no 'another session' warning; a chat that left without handover still triggers it. `brain route` itself still reads the manifest's tier (route.py, package G).
For a request routed as resume, boot's recall query is the recorded item, next and blockers; with nothing recorded, recall is skipped.
Without --next, what was finished or is now in progress leaves the next list (a bare id matches its titled entry). `--next ''` empties the list and the help says so.

push_brain_records commits only this session's inbox files and the radar state, honours BRAIN_NO_PUSH and BRAIN_NO_NETWORK for a remote that is not a local folder (no commit, no push attempt), never pushes from a checkout under the system temp folder or a scratchpad path, and its line says what went where. The --push help names the brain repository. No override variable was added: a scratch copy with a local remote still pushes, which is what tests need.
